messages.content: Write the welcome page new engineers see on their first day at a software company. Around 250 words.

output:
# Welcome

You're here. Someone will hand you a laptop in the next hour, and after that the day is mostly yours.

Start with `setup.sh` in the platform repo. It installs the toolchain, pulls a scrubbed copy of the staging database, and takes about twenty minutes on decent wifi. It will fail at least once — that's expected, and the fix is almost always in the troubleshooting section at the bottom of the README. If it isn't, ask in #dev-help. People answer there fast.

Your onboarding buddy will find you before lunch. They've blocked out Tuesday and Thursday afternoons this week, so save the questions that need a whiteboard.

One thing worth saying up front: we expect your first pull request by Friday. Not a big one. Fix a typo in the docs, delete a dead flag, tighten an error message. The point is to walk the whole path — branch, review, CI, deploy — while it's still low-stakes enough that breaking something is funny rather than expensive.

You will not understand the codebase this month. Nobody does. There are eleven services, and most engineers here have a working mental model of three or four. Learn yours deeply and trust your colleagues on the rest.

A few habits that make life here easier. Write the design doc before the code, even when it's four paragraphs. Say "I don't know" early. Push back on a review comment if you disagree with it — silent compliance costs us more than an argument does.

Coffee's on the second floor. Go find it.
